newsitem.title: TAJIKISTAN: Tajik rebel army colonel takes town, officials say.
newsitem.headline: Tajik rebel army colonel takes town, officials say.

text.p: A rebel colonel has taken control of a large area of southwestern Tajikistan and is demanding changes to a peace deal between the government and the Islamic opposition, Tajik military officials said on Thursday.

"Colonel Makhmud Khudoyberdyev said today that he controls the town of Kurgan Tyube and the adjoining area," a senior Tajik military official told Reuters in the capital Dushanbe. The government of the former Soviet republic and the Islamic opposition signed a peace deal last month to end a four-year civil war.

"Khudoyberdyev said he still backs the president and the government and is ready to take part in the process of national reconciliation but demands that some points in the peace agreement with the opposition be revised," the official said.

He said Khudoyberdyev, whose elite armoured brigade is based in Kurgan Tyube and numbers around 1,500 servicemen backed by tanks and armoured personnel carriers, strongly opposed the return of 460 armed Islamic guerrillas to Dushanbe.
The guerrillas are due to return to the capital soon under last month's peace agreement, which provides for opposition participation in all power structures and for new parliamentary elections.

A military official said there was no shooting or disorder in Kurgan Tyube, which is the administrative centre of the Khatlon region and is located about 100 km (60 miles) southwest of Dushanbe. Khudoyberdyev could not be reached for comment.
